banner: Operations only: equipment, checklists, sterilisation and handover. Ustaad never gives diagnosis or treatment advice — ask the treating doctor.
llm_guard: NEVER give medical diagnosis, drug doses or treatment advice. If asked, say this must come from the treating doctor. Only equipment, process, checklist and handover knowledge.
safety_line: Patient safety first: switch to the backup device before troubleshooting, and follow the manufacturer's instructions.

records.symptom: Ventilator alarming 'high blower temperature' at night; backup ventilator connected by ICU team
records.cause: Inlet air filter clogged with dust
records.action: Swapped in backup ventilator; replaced the inlet filter; ran the manufacturer's self-test before return to service
records.source_ref: Matches FDA MAUDE reports: 'replacement of the filter resolved' high blower temperature

records.symptom: Battery icon not charging; internal battery under 20% after a power cut
records.cause: Internal battery at end of life (3 years)
records.action: Replaced internal battery; logged battery date on the asset sticker; set a 30-month replacement reminder

records.symptom: Pre-use check fails at flow sensor calibration

records.cause: Moisture inside the expiratory flow sensor
records.action: Replaced the expiratory flow sensor; recalibrated; pre-use check passed

records.cause: Roller clamp partly closed and line kinked under the patient's arm
records.action: Opened roller clamp fully; re-routed the line; checked line from bag to cannula

records.symptom: Accuracy check on a landmark shows about 4 mm error
records.cause: Patient reference array bumped while draping
records.action: Stopped; re-registered; re-checked accuracy on two landmarks before the surgeon continued

records.cause: Main lamp past its rated hours
records.action: Switched to the backup lamp from the panel; replaced main lamp after the case; logged lamp hours

records.symptom: Bipolar forceps not coagulating, unit shows no fault
records.cause: Bipolar cable broken inside the insulation near the connector
records.action: Swapped the bipolar cable with a spare; tested with a continuity check; condemned the old cable

records.symptom: Morning Bowie-Dick test sheet shows uneven colour change
records.action: Stopped loads; replaced door gasket; ran leak test and repeated Bowie-Dick test — passed

records.cause: Chamber overloaded; packs touching the walls
records.action: Loaded fewer packs; kept gaps between them; used full drying time

records.symptom: Night shift did not know a pump had been changed in the evening
records.action: Started bedside SBAR handover (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) with an equipment line

records.symptom: Mysuru ventilator alarming high blower temperature
records.action: Followed Prakash's fix from Ustaad (Bengaluru): replaced the inlet filter; self-test passed
Followed Prakash's fix from Ustaad: checked door gasket, replaced, repeated test — passed

records.symptom: Landmark check off by about 3 mm after repositioning the camera

tips.text: High blower temperature alarm on our ICU ventilators: first look at the inlet air filter — dust-blocked filters are the usual cause. Replace it and run the self-test before blaming the blower.
Run the Bowie-Dick test every morning in the first empty cycle of a pre-vacuum autoclave. If the colour change is uneven, there is air in the chamber — check the door gasket before running any load.
Steam sterilisation needs at least 121 °C for 15 minutes or 134 °C for 3 minutes at the right pressure. Never shorten the drying time to save a cycle — wet packs are not sterile.
After draping or moving the camera, always do a landmark accuracy check. If the reference array was touched, re-register — don't let the case continue on an old registration.
Use SBAR at the bedside for every handover and add one equipment line: which pumps or ventilators were changed, alarms seen, and what is pending with biomedical.

WHO Time Out before skin incision: everyone says name and role; confirm patient, procedure and side on the displayed images; antibiotic within 60 minutes; anticipated critical events; confirm sterility indicators.

checklists.title: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist + Neuro OT additions
checklists.source: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist (2009). Lines marked 'Neuro OT' are this demo hospital's own additions.

phases.name: Sign In — before anaesthesia
items: Patient has confirmed identity, site, procedure and consent
Site marked
Anaesthesia safety check completed
Pulse oximeter on the patient and working
Known allergy?
Difficult airway or aspiration risk?
Risk of >500 ml blood loss (7 ml/kg in children)?

phases.name: Time Out — before skin incision
items: All team members introduced by name and role
Confirm patient name, procedure and where the incision will be made
Antibiotic prophylaxis given within the last 60 minutes?
Anticipated critical events reviewed (surgeon, anaesthetist, nursing)
Sterility (including indicator results) confirmed; any equipment issues?
Essential imaging displayed
Neuro OT: side confirmed on the displayed scan
Neuro OT: navigation accuracy checked on a landmark
Neuro OT: microscope draped, balanced, backup lamp OK

phases.name: Sign Out — before the patient leaves the OT
items: Name of the procedure recorded
Instrument, sponge and needle counts complete
Specimen labelled (with patient name)
Equipment problems to be addressed
Key concerns for recovery handed over
Neuro OT: any equipment issue logged in Ustaad
